cells.tense: You are carrying what is yours to carry, and it is not bending you.
cells.ask: Put one thing that has held up under you in front of someone who needs it, then let yourself stop carrying that piece.
cells.core:
You can hold weight that stays weight. Things get set down on you — other people's asking, work that has to keep standing, the plain weight of a day — and you take it without going rigid and without folding. Most people either break or turn hard. You do neither.

What is working now is that you are still in the room. You are in touch with what you are holding instead of braced against it, so the strength stays usable instead of turning into armor. Something in you wants to go further: to stay close to people while the weight is on you, so what is heavy is also shared. Try it once today. Pick something that has already proved it holds, hand it to someone who needs it, and after it is out of your hands, notice what they do with it. Let the empty minute be real. Then see what your hands want next.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what is yours without bending, and that is a rare strength.
cells.verb: bearing weight that has to be borne
cells.place: where holding capacity is built and spent

cells.tense: You are already carrying what has not arrived, and the carrying is ahead of the need.
cells.ask: Pick one load that is not yet on you and leave it with whoever it belongs to until it actually comes.
cells.core:
You are bracing ahead of the load. Something is coming — a demand, a problem, a thing that might break — and you take its shape early, lifting before it is on you, in case you are not enough when it lands. The muscle is tightening around a weight that is not there yet.

That is the same strength that works, aimed at the wrong hour. Bracing steals the hours the thing is not here. What you need now is not more grip. It is the sense that give and take can run both ways — that what belongs to someone else can stay with them, and your share will be enough when it arrives. Pick one load that is not yet on you and leave it where it belongs until it actually comes. What is on your plate today stays exactly as heavy. The difference is what is not on it.

cells.tense: You once stopped taking on more, and you are still where that decision left you.
cells.ask: Finish one thing you already started and say out loud that it is done, then start something small and let it stay small.
cells.core:
Something got set down a while back and has not been picked up again. You stopped reaching for what needs holding — said it was fine, said it was handled, and moved around it. The strength did not go anywhere. You are just not putting it to work right now.

There is a door behind you and you are sitting at it. What is needed is not another push into the weight. It is finishing something and letting it be finished — a completed thing gives back the strength you spent on it instead of asking for more. Finish one thing you already started and say out loud that it is done. Then start something small and let it stay small. You are not here to hold everything. You are here to hold what is yours until it is done.
cells.sheetLine: You put the weight down once and did not pick it back up.

cells.tense: You are holding up more than you say, and you do not call it holding.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are already carrying that you have been calling just what you do — once, to yourself, in plain words.
cells.core:
It is already happening. You are the one people set things on, the one who stays standing when the room tilts, and you talk about it like the sun coming up — just how things are, nothing special, nobody in particular doing it. The strength is working for you all day and the person it belongs to gives it no credit.

That is not modesty. It is a pen put down. You are building something that lasts — a steadiness others lean on — and you call it nothing because it comes easily. What comes easily to you was paid for somewhere. Try this once: name one thing you are already carrying that you have been calling just what you do. Say it to yourself in plain words.

The weight is already there. You can claim it.
cells.sheetLine: You are already the one holding it up. You just don't say so.
